subgroup" behaviour. The scope follows the SEARCH TEXT only, not the Hide decoys
or Hide contaminants checkboxes, so hiding rows for display never silently drops a
family from a recluster. Clear the Search box and both act on the whole database
again, exactly as before. Locks still hold within the subgroup.

WHY DIVIDE AND CONQUER GIVES A FLOOR, NOT A RECOMMENDATION
---------------------------------------------------------
Divide and Conquer searches for the lowest sequence identity at which no family
holds both a target and a decoy sequence. It is tempting to read its answer as
"the right identity". It is not, for a reason built into what the score can see.

A reversed database has the same internal redundancy as the real one: if two
proteins are similar, their reversed copies are similar too. So decoy families
collapse at the same rate as target families, and putting two decoys together is
not an error. The only event the score can detect is a target aligning to a decoy,
which happens once alignments have stopped being better than noise.

It therefore marks the identity below which clustering is meaningless. It CANNOT
see two unrelated target families being fused, which is the error you actually
care about. The number it gives you is a floor, not a recommendation.

So: cluster at that identity or above, and
choose the exact value from "Scan identity range" and from the biology of your
proteins. Raising the allowance above 0 does not buy accuracy, it buys merges made
inside the noise.

THE OTHER COLUMNS
-----------------
USearch ID       the last automatic grouping (USearch, then any reclustering the
                 program ran). Read-only. It equals User ID except where you
                 renumbered a family by hand.
User ID          your own family number. Editable: change it and the families are
                 regrouped, the User column recalculated, and it is the number
                 written back by Analysis > Reannotate SEPro.
User Annotation  free text, saved in the .fcf and exported. It also NAMES the family
                 in the Full XIC composition CSV, the Results chart and the
                 evidence pack. A family without one is named by the protein name
                 most of its members share (read before "OS=", "(Fragment)"
                 ignored); a tie follows the stored member order, not the grid sort.
Locus            a UniProt accession where available, otherwise the database identifier.
                 Hover over a cell for the full original identifier, kept in the file.
Residue mass     the sum of the protein's amino-acid residue masses, in daltons.
                 It does NOT include the terminal water: add 18.011 Da for the
                 neutral protein, and 1.007 Da more for the protonated (MH+) mass.
                 The column used to be called "Monoisotopic MH", which this number
                 has never been.

THE FAMILY COUNTER AND THE FILTERS
----------------------------------
The counter reads "N visible · M in file". Display and export filters hide rows,
they never change a number: hiding decoys or contaminants lowers the visible count
and leaves every percentage exactly as it was. In "% of identified signal" the hidden rows
are still inside the denominator, because that denominator is the sum over all
families, filtered or not.
Decoys are hidden by default; Show automatic IDs reveals the retained USearch ID.
Hide contaminants matches the case-sensitive prefix 'contaminant_', after one optional 'Reverse_' prefix.
It includes labelled keratins, trypsin and serum proteins; hiding them affects the
table and visible-row CSV only, so visible identified-signal shares can total below 100%.

Export to CSV writes exactly the rows you can see, with the values as fractions
between 0 and 1 and a dot as the decimal separator, whatever your machine's
language is. That is on purpose: the file is meant to be read by a program.

FILES, NAVIGATION AND KEYBOARD
Start actions also have menu commands; the status bar names the current stage and open project and explains what to do next. Tab and Shift+Tab move between enabled controls, and the native focus indicator marks the active control.

If no project is open, nothing is saved: use File > Open for a .fqproj or .fcf, or File > New from database to build families. File and row counts use whole numbers with digit grouping and no decimal places.

File > Save keeps families, User IDs, annotations and computed quantitation together in one .fqproj; use Save as to keep the previous version. The .fcf export keeps the families and annotations without the full XIC result.

Results reads stored full-envelope quantitation, including family shares and total-ion-current recovery, without reading RAW or changing families. Compute full XIC first when the project has no stored quantitation, then save the project to keep it.

The spectrum comparison is read-only, with one row per file, scan, charge and precursor m/z hypothesis, comparing PEAKS, DeepNovo and PatternLab. Its CSV export names the written CSV path in the completion message.


CURATION AND FAMILY SHARES
The recorded identity is the threshold used to build the file; higher identity gives more, smaller families, and changing it requires a new Build run. Align selected opens an alignment in a new window to check whether the selected family members are homologous.

Fetch evidence needs internet when the requested facts are not already cached; retrieved Pfam domains fill Domains, can be found by Search and can be selected in the grouping preview. Saving keeps them in the file, and family numbers stay unchanged by fetching.

Recluster by words merges descriptions meeting the similarity threshold, from 0.10 to 1.00; default 0.95 keeps near-identical wording, and lower it towards 0.90 to gather related descriptions. Family numbers change and percentages are recalculated; Undo restores the previous curation.

Ignore words accepts commas or spaces and is useful when a common word pulls unrelated families together. Ctrl+A selects all rows in the filtered protein view; Ctrl or Shift selects individual rows or ranges for User ID and annotation edits.

PatternLab projects must be exported at PEPTIDE level; a protein-level export makes every row read 0. The optional PatternLab share column stays empty until a project is loaded in PatternLab (optional), and Recalculate is unavailable until then.

For Full XIC, quantified signal gives family composition and total ion current gives each family's share of the whole sample, using the summed TIC of every recorded run. A Full XIC basis change applies at once.

The Full XIC summary accounts for families, peptides shared between families and peptides with no family. Export family composition writes CSV with one row per family and an unattributed row; its shared-peptide row appears only with Family-unique only.

Show quantified families only starts off and hides unquantified families without changing percentages. Hide decoys hides identifiers starting with Reverse_ from the table and CSV, without deleting data or changing percentages; show them while judging the clustering.

Manage locks is unavailable while no family is locked; removing a lock changes the open file immediately, and saving keeps it on disk. Apply grouping gathers the ticked proteins into one family and can be reversed with Undo; it is unavailable when there is no change to apply.



FAMILY PANEL AND EVIDENCE

File > Import family panel opens a draft for the open project. Choose a
spreadsheet, sheet and header row, then select the family key, name and
decision columns and, optionally, a Pfam column. Map every source decision
to Quantify, Report under others, Not a family or Merge into family. A merge
names the target family key. Preview the panel before applying it. Source
column text and the chosen mappings stay with the panel.

Keys must be unique within their scope. Add, edit or remove family rows in
the table. Multiple Pfam and subclass keys are separated by semicolons.
Unchanged keys keep their existing domain and subclass details.
Save panel as spreadsheet writes a reusable template. Its Families and
Subclasses sheets can be edited and imported again; the template also
retains panel details not shown in those sheets. The Subclasses sheet can
hold required and absent Pfam codes, source subfamily text and a report-as
key. Apply panel commits one project change; Undo can restore the prior
panel. Later assignment or subclass refresh operations have their own
Undo steps. Save the project to retain the change.

Check Pfam compares the panel's accessions and supplied names with the
provider. A mismatch, missing entry or unavailable check is shown; it
never silently changes the panel. A missing domain call is not proof that
a domain is absent.

Evidence grouping proposes family assignments from stored source evidence
and reviewed neighbours. Review and confirm ambiguous links between source
contexts and panel families, including an explicit outside-panel choice.
Apply only the proposals you accept. Unassigned or conflicting cases stay
visible rather than being guessed. Changing relevant panel rules can make
assignments and subclass labels out of date; rebuild them before use.

Subclass rules use the panel's required and absent domains or source
subfamily text. A fragment or missing evidence may not establish an
absence. Tied or incompatible evidence stays unresolved. A protein label
alone does not make a peptide unique to that subclass: shared peptide
evidence remains at the family or unresolved level when it cannot
distinguish a subclass.

FAMILY NUMBERS AND FIGURES

The composition headline is the mean of available per-run shares of the
signal credited to database families. The measured peptide signal and RAW
total ion current (TIC) are separate denominators; a peptide-signal share
is not a TIC share. Family-world-only signal is shown separately and is
not added to the database-family composition. These are signal shares,
not direct measurements of sample mass.

Run-to-run spread is the sample standard deviation, available only with
at least two runs. CV is that standard deviation divided by the mean and
is unavailable when the mean is zero. A run with a zero denominator has
an unavailable share, not zero. A pooled share sums signal across runs
before dividing and can differ from the mean of available per-run shares.
Where a measured-signal or TIC summary requires every run, missing values
leave that summary unavailable.

The protein count is a greedy estimate of the database proteins needed
to explain the observed peptides, not an exact minimum and not a gene
or proteoform count. A protein with a peptide of its own has an exactly
contained peptide unique among database targets, including labelled
contaminants; decoys are not targets. Shared evidence can support the
greedy explanation; homology-only matches can remain
unexplained. Read the unexplained count beside the estimate. Abundance
and the number of explanatory proteins answer different questions.

A family goes to Others when its mean share is strictly below the report
threshold, or when its panel decision is Report under others. The default
threshold is 0.1 percent and can be changed in Export report. The
member list retains the individual families and the reason for grouping.
Excluded panel rows are not families. A numeric family that conflicts
between panel keys or mixes panel and outside members stays a separate
flagged row rather than being assigned or added to Others.

Sensitivity comparisons, when stored, show how results change with the
selected shared-peptide policy and de novo cutoff. A missing combination
is unavailable, not an invented result. Count in every family overlaps:
those contributions cannot be summed as a normalized composition.

Family bars show mean shares with sample-SD whiskers when available.
Subclass stacks and the family/subclass ring use their stated pooled
basis; read their captions rather than equating pooled values with run
means. When available, the ring uses the same Others membership as the
report. The
abundance-versus-diversity plot pairs share with the greedy protein
estimate. A coverage map shows the stored protein positions, domains and
supported peptide placements; missing or ambiguous positions stay
unavailable or unresolved. The signal-source figure separates identified,
database-matched de novo and family-world-only contributions. Other
quality figures retain their own denominators and captions.

REPORT AND SUPPLEMENT

File > Report details stores the title, authors, sample description,
workflow, database kind and your written interpretation in the project.
Recorded input provenance is shown there. The interpretation is your own
text; check that any numbers it quotes are present in the report.

File > Export report needs stored Results. Choose sections and figures;
clearing a section removes its contents, and clearing a figure removes
that figure. The choices and report threshold can be saved in the project.
The report uses the project's own facts and the Light export palette.
Missing studies are identified as unavailable rather than filled in.
When a companion supplement is produced, use it for the long tables and
the individual families grouped as Others. Exporting a report does not
save the project: use File > Save to retain the choices and details for
a later export.
","dnActual":"THE DE NOVO EVIDENCE SCREEN
===========================
Selected source: PEAKS de novo only (*.denovoOnly.csv; ALC (%)).

A separate workflow, not a step of the family one. It needs no Family Cluster
File to start, it changes no family, no User ID and no quantitation, and it
writes nothing except the CSV files you ask it for. It asks which de novo calls
pass their source-specific filters and how comparable precursor hypotheses relate
to the PatternLab search.

Nothing on this screen interrupts you with a dialog. A parameter it cannot
accept, a folder with no export in it, a file that will not open: all of them
are reported in the status line at the bottom, and the previous value or the
previous result is left in force.

THE ORDER OF WORK
-----------------
This screen has two core steps, and an optional advanced section below them.

Step 1, Import and filter, reads the selected de novo export and keeps the confident
sequences. Step 2, Reconcile and review, compares them with a PatternLab search
of the SAME runs and lists comparable-precursor alternative hypotheses and weak
agreements as a review queue.
That queue is the one thing only this screen produces.

Quantify (Analysis > Compute full XIC) uses the selected sources and shared filters for full
XIC computation and reported by Results through the .fqproj project, so the
de novo set no longer has to carry the whole story on its own.

The collapsed Standalone homology (advanced) section maps the kept peptide
sequences against a family file. It needs neither quantitation nor an open
project, and it can run straight after Import and filter. After the search,
open Results, choose Homology assignments (CSV), and press Export. Results
retains that completed snapshot independently of full XIC.

WHAT THE SELECTED SOURCE LIST IS
--------------------------------
PEAKS de novo only writes one *.denovoOnly.csv export per run.
These are spectra sequenced from fragments alone that the PEAKS database
search did not identify. This is an export category, not proof that the
sequence is correct or biologically novel.

A sequence read this way carries no protein and no statistical support from a
search engine. It carries PEAKS de novo only's own ALC (%), which is why this screen
starts with a filter rather than with a count.

The folder is searched recursively, so the folder holding the per-run
sub-folders is the right one to give, and every run of the export is read
together. Runs are named by their FILE NAME everywhere on this screen, never by
their position in a folder or in a project: a de novo export, a directory listing
and a PatternLab project are not in the same order, and pairing them by
position joins every spectrum against the wrong acquisition.

THE THREE DE NOVO QUALITY FILTERS
---------------------------------
A row is kept only if it clears all three. The third filter uses two boxes.

Minimum length (7 residues)
    A short call carries too little information to be matched against a
    protein afterwards. Lowering this is what turns the homology step of
    standalone homology into a random-match generator.

Minimum ALC (80%)
    ALC is PEAKS' average local confidence: the mean of the per-residue
    confidences of one call. It is the blunt filter; the local-confidence
    stretch below asks a different question. It is an operational threshold,
    not a calibrated de novo FDR, and it is not interchangeable with another
    caller's score.

Stretch length (5 residues) and stretch floor (90%)
    One criterion in two boxes, and the sharp one: somewhere in the sequence
    there must be a run of that many CONSECUTIVE residues, each of them at
    or above that confidence. A residue below the floor breaks the run. This
    is what keeps the sequence with one trustworthy region and drops the one
    a global score can flatter; it complements rather than replaces the
    source-native score cutoff.

Counts depend on the selected source and cutoffs. The counters on this screen show the loaded data,
including how many rows were read and kept; the per-run breakdown shows each acquisition.
Loosening the filters is a decision about how much uncertain sequence you carry
into every later step. The
per-run breakdown under the counters is where to look for a run that behaved
differently from the others.

THE FIVE VERDICTS, IN PLAIN LANGUAGE
------------------------------------
Reconcile first joins by normalized acquisition file and MS2 scan. It then requires
the same reported charge and precursor m/z within 20 ppm, isotope-error-aware so
the M, M+-1 and M+-2 selections of one precursor match, before comparing sequences.
Each filtered row from the selected source receives one of five verdicts:

De novo only        nothing in the search shares that spectrum. This is new
                    relative to PatternLab at the file-and-scan level; the
                    current screen reports the count for the loaded source.
Different precursor the scan is shared, but no PatternLab PSM has both the same
context             charge and m/z within 20 ppm. No sequence comparison is made.
Redundant equal     same file, scan, charge, m/z and sequence once the notation
                    is normalised. It only confirms what PatternLab has.
Equal but weak PSM  same comparable precursor and sequence, but PatternLab's own
                    cross-correlation is below the threshold.
Overlapping         same file, scan, charge and m/z, but a different sequence.
alternative         It is excluded from additive de novo quantification and kept
                    for review. It is not a database-search accuracy estimate.

The loaded data determines how many rows share a file and scan, then a charge and
20-ppm precursor m/z, before strict or I/L-folded sequence comparison. Read the
on-screen counters and comparison table for the current source and cutoffs.

The different-precursor-context verdict is worth understanding. A mass spectrometer
isolates a window, not a molecule, so two species eluting together are
fragmented into ONE spectrum: a chimeric spectrum. PatternLab explained one of
them; the de novo call may be an alternative ion in that window. The scan number
alone cannot establish duplication, sequence conflict, or biological truth.

That is why scan number alone is never used to claim equality. Charge and m/z are
explicit gates; failing either means a different precursor context, not a conflict.

THE DATABASE-SEARCH AGREEMENT CONTROL
-------------------------------------
The valid search-vs-search control compares PatternLab PSMs with PEAKS db.psms,
not with a de novo export. It compares shared file+scan keys, reported charge and
exact sequence after removing PTM notation. The counts and agreement percentages
depend on the loaded searches; use the loaded project's database-search concordance table.

THE REVIEW QUEUE, AND WHY IT IS MANUAL
--------------------------------------
The queue holds exactly two of the five verdicts: overlapping alternatives, and
agreements where PatternLab's own evidence was weak. The other three are
results, and a result does not need a decision.

An overlapping alternative is a de novo hypothesis on a comparable precursor.
Nothing in either
answer decides which is right: a cross-correlation and ALC (%) are not on the
same scale, are not calibrated against each other, and are not measuring the
same thing. An automatic rule here would be an invented threshold dressed as a
result, and it would be invisible afterwards.

So the program presents the evidence and decides nothing. The table is
read-only and shows both sequences side by side with the cross-correlation on
the PatternLab side and ALC (%) plus the weakest residue confidence on the de
novo side, plus how far apart the two precursors were in ppm. It is a
review set for the loaded source. Export it and
the evidence can be inspected away from this screen. These rows are not added to
the de novo signal while unresolved, so review cannot inflate quantification.

An equal-but-weak row is retained in the review export rather than labelled as an
ordinary redundant confirmation. It is excluded from additive de novo quantification
until reviewed, so the evidence remains visible without double-counting its signal.

The following legacy definitions remain as scientific reference for old files.
Their standalone extraction and partition controls were retired from De novo
in 2.0; use Quantify and Results for full XIC.

LEGACY EXTRACTION SEMANTICS (REFERENCE)
----------------------------------------
The legacy extraction engine opens a run's RAW once and integrates every kept
precursor, at its own anchor scan. The acquisitions are found BY FILE NAME, one
run is held in memory at a time, and the results are cached beside the RAW
files so a second session over the same runs costs seconds instead of minutes.

M+0 is the monoisotopic peak alone: the isotope that carries no heavy carbon.
The whole isotope envelope (M+0 plus M+1 plus M+2) is measured beside it, but
only as a diagnostic in the legacy three-way comparison described below.
PatternLab's stored quants are M+0, and one bar cannot be built from two
different bases without saying something false about the comparison.

The counts come in TWO GRAINS and the column headings say which:

    ANCHORS   one request per MS2 scan that fired on that precursor. "Rows
              in", "unique precursors" and "with signal" are anchors.
    PEAKS     one integrated elution peak. "Distinct peaks" and every area
              are peaks.

They differ because one elution peak is usually sampled by several MS2 scans:
several anchors, one peak, and the extractor hands that same peak back to each
of them. Legacy extraction totals are summed over DISTINCT PEAKS. Summing per
anchor instead would add the same trapezoid once per MS2 event, which inflates
the ion current by a few percent, always upwards, and never fails a check. The
"redundant anchors" and "redundant area" columns report exactly what that
mistake would have added.

The "shared-window bound" column is a BOUND, not a correction. Two peaks of the
same precursor inside one extraction window can be two genuine elution events
across a long gradient, or one broad peak entered twice; telling them apart
needs each peak's scan span, which this extraction does not record. So they are
all kept, and the most that could still be double-counted (each window's total
less its largest peak) is printed instead of being quietly removed.

WHAT STANDALONE HOMOLOGY MAPS
--------------------------------------
A de novo sequence has no protein attached. Standalone homology asks whether it looks
like one anyway: each DISTINCT kept sequence is aligned against the proteins of
a Family Cluster File, and every surviving hit is attributed to the User ID
family of the protein it landed in. One file answers both halves, which is why
a hit can never land in a protein the family table does not know.

The sequences are deduplicated first: the same tag read in fifty spectra is one
alignment, not fifty, so "peptides searched" is far below the rows kept in
Import and filter. The minimum identity is a PREFILTER, not the score: a protein that
never reaches that fraction of literal identity is never aligned at all.
Isoleucine and leucine are treated as one residue there by default, because
they have the same mass and a fragment spectrum cannot tell them apart, so
punishing the engine's arbitrary choice between them would be punishing physics.

WHAT THE DECOY-ONLY COUNT MEANS. It is a CONTROL, and it is not an FDR. The
family file carries reversed sequences beside the real ones. A peptide that
found only reversed proteins was attributed to something that does not exist,
so the rate of that is the rate at which this identity threshold invents a
family out of chance similarity. Read "mapped to targets" beside it and never
on its own: if the two are of the same size, the threshold is too low, whatever
the mapped number looks like alone.

It is not an FDR because nothing here is calibrated into a corrected error rate
per hit: there is no competition between a target and its decoy for one
spectrum, and no q-value is computed or implied. It is one number to read the
other against. A peptide that found both keeps its targets and drops its
decoys; a peptide that found only decoys keeps them, which is the entire point
of having them, and it stays out of the family table below.

Most kept sequences match nothing at all, and that is not a defect. They are
the reason a de novo search was run.

LEGACY THREE-WAY COMPARISON (REFERENCE)
---------------------------------------------
The legacy comparison has a bar per run and one pooled bar. It uses the WHOLE ion
current, read from the RAW with no trimming at either end, and it is cut into
three exhaustive parts:

    PatternLab   the ion current of the peptides the database search
                 identified and quantified.
    De novo      what the kept de novo set adds on top of that.
    Remainder    what is left, and still has no owner.

The three shares add up to 100% by construction, because the remainder is
defined as what the other two leave. That is arithmetic, not a result, and the
thing that had to be earned instead is COMPARABILITY: both of the first two
numerators are monoisotopic, and both count one integrated peak once.

A NEGATIVE remainder is never clamped to zero. It is a finding: it says the two
numerators together claim more signal than the run's chromatogram holds, and
hiding it would hide exactly the case worth knowing about.

THE PROVENANCE WORDS. Each number of the table carries one of three, because
the three parts arrive by three different routes and only two of them are
measurements:

    measured   computed here, from the RAW file, by the machinery named beside
               the word. The total ion current and the de novo areas are this.
    recorded   read out of a file that had written it down: a divisor recorded
               in the .plp, or the stored quants of a .xic2. The PatternLab
               part is this.
    derived    neither measured nor read, but obtained from the others by
               arithmetic. The remainder is always this, and that is why it
               can come out negative.

The word alone is not enough, so the source is printed with it: "recorded"
does not distinguish a divisor read from a .plp from quants summed out of a
.xic2, and those are different measurements of different things.

The legacy branch note records which source actually answered WORD FOR WORD,
refusals included. A project that merged its technical replicates holds one
averaged column for three acquisitions and cannot answer per run; no arithmetic
recovers what was averaged away, so it says so and the .xic2 is used instead.
Reducing that to a flag would hide which of the two you are looking at.

Every inspection or Results CSV uses a dot for the decimal separator whatever your
machine's language is. Legacy partition numbers are written in their shortest
round-trippable form, so a value read back is the same bits that were plotted.

DE NOVO WORKFLOW DETAILS
De novo review is optional inspection only and accepts one source or a union of PEAKS and DeepNovo; Quantify can combine sources and reads its de novo folder independently. Review changes no family or quantitation, so it is not needed for quantitation.

With a project, use Quantify and Results for extraction and reporting. Standalone family attribution reads peptides, not chromatograms, so it can run directly after importing and filtering the calls.

Results > Homology assignments exports CSV with one line per searched peptide, including family IDs, protein IDs and ambiguity. It is unavailable until a homology search result exists, including a result retained from an earlier search.
